title: El Viaje
focus: Past tenses, tú vs. usted, and the subjunctive for things you haven't found yet

slots.skill: Imperfect means it was in progress (maybe unfinished)
slots.mis: "Preterite and imperfect both just mean past"

slots.skill: usted with someone you just met
Answer a "what would you do" question in the conditional
slots.mis: Answers a hypothetical in the past or present

slots.skill: Switch to tú when invited (háblame de tú)
Subjunctive for something you haven't found yet
slots.mis: "The subjunctive is only for doubt and feelings"

A.q: Ana says: “Escribía el informe cuando se fue la luz.” Did she finish the report?
o: Probably not. She was in the middle of it.
A.why: Escribía = was writing. The power cut off in the middle.

A.q: You meet your host family's grandmother for the first time. What do you say?
A.why: A first meeting with an older adult: usted.

A.q: Interviewer: “¿Qué harías si perdieras el vuelo?” Best answer:
A.why: "What would you do" gets a "would" answer: the conditional.

A.q: Your new coworker says: “Por favor, háblame de tú.” Next you say:
A.why: Háblame de tú means "use tú with me." Staying formal now sounds distant.

A.q:
You don't have a hotel yet.
Busco un hotel que ___ piscina.
A.why: Any hotel with a pool, not a specific one you know: subjunctive.

B.q: Pablo says: “Pagaba la cuenta cuando sonó el teléfono.” Did he pay the bill?
o: We don't know. He was in the middle of paying.
B.why: Pagaba = was paying. The phone rang in the middle.

B.q: You need help from a hotel receptionist you've never met. What do you say?
Interviewer: “¿Qué harías con un día libre en Monterrey?” Best answer:
o: Subiría al Cerro de la Silla.
Subí al Cerro de la Silla.
Subo al Cerro de la Silla.
B.why: "What would you do" gets a "would" answer: subiría.

B.q: Your host dad says: “Aquí todos nos hablamos de tú.” At dinner you say:

You need a roommate but haven't found one.
Necesito un compañero de cuarto que ___ inglés.
B.why: Any roommate who speaks English, not a specific person: subjunctive.

postcard: Write a short email (3 to 5 sentences) to your boss in Monterrey, whom you call usted: thank her, and tell her about one problem on the trip.

rubric.title: Tells what happened
rubric.detail: Events in the preterite, scene in the imperfect

rubric.title: Right register
rubric.detail: Uses usted with the boss all the way through

rubric.title: Polite and clear request or thanks
rubric.detail: A real thank-you or request a boss would understand
